# axm auth token create

Create a granular access token

## When to use

Create a granular access token

## Usage

```bash
axm auth token create [flags]
```

## Arguments

None.

## Flags

| Name               | Type    | Required | Description                                                  |
| ------------------ | ------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--name`           | string  | No       | Human-readable token name                                    |
| `--expires`        | string  | No       | Token lifetime: 7d, 30d, 1y, or an ISO timestamp             |
| `--owner`          | string  | No       | Owner selector; repeatable. Use "all" for full surface.      |
| `--extension`      | string  | No       | Extension selector in @handle/<type>/<name> form; repeatable |
| `--permission`     | choice  | No       | Extension permission level (choices: read, publish, admin)   |
| `--org-permission` | choice  | No       | Organization permission level (choices: read, write, admin)  |
| `--cidr`           | string  | No       | CIDR allowlist entry; repeatable                             |
| `--bypass-mfa`     | boolean | No       | Allow this automation token to bypass step-up MFA            |

Global flags are documented on [Global flags](../../global-flags).

## Examples

**Create a publish token scoped to @foo**

```bash
axm token create --name ci --owner @foo --permission publish
```

**Create a read-only token**

```bash
axm token create --name read-only --permission read --expires 30d
```

## Requirements

None.

## Side effects

None.
